To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
health and social care professionals' motivations for continuing professional education are varied and include personal and professional development, career progression and job satisfaction.

1) the motivations of the HSC professionals in our study were mainly related to their personal development and their career development; 2) the HSC professionals experienced a number of challenges in relation to part-time study, which included time constraints, the balance of study, work, and family, and the challenges of learning in a higher education environment; and 3) the HSC professional students were supported by a number of different sources, including their own motivation, their employer, and their family
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the motivations and experiences of part-time health and social care professionals undertaking continuing professional education (CPE) in higher education (HE)?
the motivations and experiences of health professionals in relation to their part-time studies in higher education.
the motivations and experiences of part-time students in higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the main motivations and experiences of health professionals who undertake part-time study in HE are: to improve their professional practice; to enhance their career prospects; and to improve their own self-development.
the main motivation for continuing professional education for health and social care professionals is to maintain professional competence and standards of care.

the main motivations for health and social care professionals to study part-time in higher education are: the desire to improve patient care, to improve professional status, to gain promotion, and to gain a better salary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we aimed to identify and understand what motivates and influences the experiences of health and care professionals who study part-time in higher education (HE) in the UK.

the current literature does not support the notion that the motivation of health and social professionals to engage in continuing professional education is solely driven by a desire for career advancement.
